page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 20 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores with 1 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.2 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile that is generally average across most workloads, with some notable variations. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is categorized in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance reaches average levels. Conversely, Geekbench testing shows strong single-core and multi-core scores in the top 25%, alongside strong text processing performance. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 2045.15 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 69.81 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as Passmark CPU encryption and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, also perform within average parameters.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage, this server offers a resource-dense configuration suitable for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores or high-speed local NVMe drives. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, multi-threaded text processing, static web serving, and moderate database operations. The instance also supports basic machine learning tasks, demonstrating average performance in LLM inference for small and medium models. The shared CPU model provides a cost-efficient option for scaling multi-core applications that can tolerate shared-resource environments.
